chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the whispers (of Satan), so he said: 'O Abu Muhammad! Remember the breaking of your joints in your grave, and the departure of your loved ones from you when they bury you in your pit, and the exit of drops of water from your nostrils, and the eating of worms in your flesh, for indeed that will console you from what you are in.'
Abu Baseer said: 'By Allah, I did not remember it except that it eased from me what I was in, from the stress of the world.'

key_terms.الْوَسْوَاس: Whispers or temptations (of Satan) in the mind

ai.seo_question: How does contemplating death alleviate worldly anxiety according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes *tadhakkur al-mawt* (remembrance of death) not merely as a spiritual exercise, but as a practical psychological remedy for *waswas* (distracting whispers). By vividly contemplating the physical decay and the transient nature of worldly attachments—symbolized by the 'breaking of joints' and 'departure of loved ones'—the believer achieves *tasliya* (consolation), effectively detaching the heart from the anxieties of this world. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on using the reality of the grave (*barzakh*) as a tool for cognitive reframing and spiritual tranquility.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> of the temptations (in my mind), so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Muhammad! Remember the breaking of your bones in your grave, and the return of your loves ones from you when they bury you in your pit (grave), and the exit of drops of the water from your nostrils, and the insects eating your flesh. This will help you to overcome temptations’.
Abu Baseer said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I did not remember it except it eased from me what I was in, from the stress of the world’.
en.sarwar: 20. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Once I complained before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the disturbance of temptation in my mind. He (the Imam) said, ‘O abu Muhammad, speak (think) of your joints coming apart in your grave, and of your relatives abandoning you after your burial, worms coming out from your nose and other worms consuming your flesh; this will help you to overcome temptations.’
Abu Basir has said, ‘By Allah, whenever I did as he had told me to do I felt free from temptations.’”
